overallNotes: Jermaine Allen Booker (born 1987-11-14) is a 37-year-old ESTJ safety trainer at Feeders Supply Company's Louisville distribution center, separated father of two school-age children, living in a Shepherdsville townhouse. His three-year arc (2025-2028) moves from newly promoted safety trainer to the architect of the site's standard safety playbook. Major threads: (1) career — from launching a one-lane pilot to supervisor scorecards to peer coaches to site-wide playbook adoption after two clean peak seasons; (2) co-parenting — from hostile text fights to a shared co-parenting app to a 'tense but workable' dynamic; (3) health — chronic right knee injury, stress-eating and weight gain, followed by PT adherence and modest improvement; (4) housing — from a bare 'crash pad' townhouse to a settled home with a homework desk and grilling routine; (5) finances — tight cash flow, custody expenses, legal debt, eventually paying down debt and starting a trip savings bucket. Dominant personality traits: practical, evidence-driven, routine-dependent, quietly stubborn, protective of his people, conflict-weary. Key supporting characters: Danielle Renee Booker (estranged spouse), Kayla Denise Booker (older sister, blunt practical help), Sharon Elise Pruitt (EHS mentor/ally), Ramon Luis Ortega (skeptical dock supervisor), Darius Wayne Henson (close friend, honest feedback), Marcus Lee Benton (coworker, open gym connection). DATA QUALITY ISSUES: Every focus field is truncated mid-sentence (mostly 'A lot has shifted lately…' style openings). Many summaries are quote fragments rather than actual summaries. Tags are consistently too broad (work, family, housing) across all slices, missing specific searchable keywords. The emotional_tone field defaults to 'neutral' on every slice regardless of actual valence. The decisions field sometimes contains content errors (e.g., 2025-02-08 decisions mention Ramon when the correct person is Kayla). Some decisions are truncated mid-sentence. Strands.json is well-structured with 9 categories but tags would benefit from the granularity in this enrichment.
